gaps.term: outside work as a fixed number of address-field row additions
gaps.quote: The outside work is a fixed number of address-field row additions.
gaps.note: The page cites only the cost of an address interchange, O(V u^tau). It then asserts without argument that the outside work is a fixed number of row additions, and that a row addition costs O(V(u^tau+1)). The reader cannot check why the cited interchange bound transfers to row additions, or why the outside work is a fixed number of them.

gaps.quote: Taking $\lambda$ with $\log_m(s/W)<\lambda<1$ makes the ratio below 1
gaps.note: This choice of lambda must also exceed tau(1+eta/vartheta), the condition stated earlier for the outside work, and lambda must be below 1. The page never shows that these constraints can hold together. That needs tau(1+eta/vartheta)<1, which the page does not give, so the claimed exponent lambda<1 is not established.

gaps.quote: Each leaf is handled by one kernel per chunk, at cost $O(f/m^\nu)$.
gaps.note: The page does not say what a kernel is (a base-case routine, a convolution kernel and an operating-system kernel are all possible readings). It also does not say whether the cost O(f/m^nu) is per kernel or per leaf, and the later leaf cost O((s/W)^nu u) depends on which.

gaps.quote: The leaves at depth $\nu$ have $u=f/m^\nu<d^\vartheta$ chunks
gaps.note: Earlier the page sets u = f Omega bits, the field width in bits. Here u is a count of chunks, f/m^nu, and the page does not say the letter changes meaning. The reader cannot tell whether the leaf cost O((s/W)^nu u) and the bound (f/u)^sigma use bits or chunks.

gaps.term: bound on the leaf cost with d
gaps.note: This needs d to be a fixed constant, so that d^(vartheta(1-sigma)) is absorbed and f^sigma is at most f^lambda since sigma is below lambda. The page never says d is fixed; it says eta and vartheta are fixed but not d. The only bound it gives on d is d at most f^(1/vartheta), which yields only f^sigma times f^(1-sigma), that is f, not f^lambda.
